# Adjudication Task — Chapter 879

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃879화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|사람이 많으면 떠도는 말도 많아진다.
  6|
  7|천하의 중심이자 대국의 새로운 황도(皇都)로 자리 잡은 절강성 항주 역시 예외는 아니었다.
  8|
  9|아니, 오히려 가장 심한 축에 속했다.
 10|
 11|항주 어느 곳을 가더라도 누군가에게 들었던 소문을 침까지 튀겨 가며 사실인 양 읊어 대는 사람들이 득실거렸다.
 12|
 13|그들은 나는 새도 떨어트린다는 고관대작이 새로 들였다는 애첩의 미모에 대해 떠들었고, 그가 애첩에게 값비싼 패물을 선물하기 위해 백성의 고혈을 쥐어짰다는 이야기에 분노했으며, 금의위가 이미 조사에 착수했다는 소식에 연신 건배를 외쳤다.
 14|
 15|“역시 이럴 때는 금의위만큼 든든한 존재가 없지. 폐륜까지 저지르며 황위에 오르긴 했지만 그래도 일 처리 하나는 확실…….”
 16|
 17|“쉿, 그 방정맞은 주둥이 좀 닥치게. 한데 그 영감 아들 중에 한 명이 금의위라고 하지 않았었나?”
 18|
 19|“그랬지.”
 20|
 21|“그런데 그걸 걸려? 금의위에 연줄이 있는데도?”
 22|
 23|“아, 그놈. 그렇지 않아도 얼마 전에 잘렸다는군.”
 24|
 25|“그래? 왜?”
 26|
 27|“몰라. 무슨 비밀 임무라도 맡았는지 한 달 전쯤부터 안 보이더니, 며칠 전에 얼굴이 퉁퉁 부은 채로 복귀했다더라고.”
 28|
 29|“퉁퉁 부어?”
 30|
 31|“그래. 무슨 잘못을 저질렀는지 호되게 처맞은 모양이야.”
 32|
 33|누군가의 입에서 흘러나온 이야기는 금세 스쳐 지나갔다.
 34|
 35|명승고적에서 영감을 얻고자 하는 시인 묵객. 향락의 도시라 불리는 항주를 위해 천릿길을 달려온 한량.
 36|
 37|값싼 화주와 만두를 시킨 후 조용히 술잔을 기울이는 가난한 선비와 불룩 나온 배를 두드리는 부유한 장사치까지.
 38|
 39|항주에는 수많은 인간군상이 존재했고, 그들은 각자 보고 들은 것들을 마음껏 떠들어 댔다.
 40|
 41|“드디어 서호(西湖)에 가 봤으니 당장 죽어도 여한이 없어. 마음 같아서는 항주에서 일 년만 더 머무르고 싶군.”
 42|
 43|“돌아가려면 아직 달포도 더 남았는데 뭐가 걱정인가? 천천히 둘러보고 떠나기 전에 주산군도(舟山群島)에도 한번 가 보자고.”
 44|
 45|“주산군도라면, 혹시 보타산(普陀山)이라도 보러 갈 생각인가?”
 46|
 47|“맞네. 내가 부처를 믿는 것은 아니지만 그런 명산이 근처에 있다면 기왕 온 김에 한 번쯤은 가 봐야지.”
 48|
 49|“하지만 그곳에 있는 여승들은 강호인이나 다름없다던데…….”
 50|
 51|“보타암(普陀庵)의 비구니들을 말하는 거라면 걱정할 필요 없네. 황도가 이전되면서 항주의 무림인들을 솎아 내면서부터 자취를 감춘 지 벌써 십 년도 넘었다더군.”
 52|
 53|명승고적을 탐방하기 위해 항주를 찾은 시인 묵객들의 대화는 비교적 분위기가 좋았다. 가까운 곳에 자리 잡은 상인들은 좋지 않은 표정으로 연신 술을 들이붓고 있었으니까.
 54|
 55|“요새 사천 쪽 분위기가 심상치 않아. 물품들의 시세가 예측 불가 수준으로 요동치는 바람에 손해가 이만저만이 아니야.”
 56|
 57|“하면 그 소문이 사실인가? 곧 청해(海省) 땅으로부터 외적들이 물밀듯이 몰려올 거라던데. 그 때문에 청해성에 자리 잡은 곤륜파도 풍전등화의 위기고.”
 58|
 59|“외적은 무슨. 기껏해야 강호의 무뢰배, 그것도 마귀에 단단히 홀린 광신도들 아닌가. 이름만 그럴듯하게 바꿨을 뿐이지 결국 과거의 마교가 그랬듯이 중원 무림 문파에 박살 날 거야. 이번에도 금위군이 나설 필요도 없을걸.”
 60|
 61|“자네, 요 몇 년간 항주에서만 지내다 보니 세상 돌아가는 꼴을 몰라도 너무 모르는군.”
 62|
 63|“응? 무슨 정보라도 들었나?”
 64|
 65|“내가 오래전부터 지내던 무림인이 현재 무림맹 소속인데…… 과거 마교가 쳐들어왔을 때보다 훨씬 더 심각한 상황이야.”
 66|
 67|“뭐? 그 정도란 말인가?”
 68|
 69|“이미 몇 달 전에 사천에서 벌어진 사건만 봐도 모르겠나? 무려 일 만에 가까운 대병력이 모여 한바탕 혈전을 벌였어. 이 정도면 단순히 무림 내부의 분쟁이 아니라 소국 간의 전쟁이라고 봐도 무방하지.”
 70|
 71|“……!”
 72|
 73|“그뿐만이 아닐세. 아직 정확히 확인된 것은 아니지만 운남(雲南)에서도 모종의 움직임이 포착됐어.”
 74|
 75|“운남? 설마 남만의 그 오랑캐들?”
 76|
 77|“맞네. 남만야수궁이 모든 전력을 동원하여 중원으로 북상 중이라더군. 그 소문이 사실이라면 지금쯤 사천이나 광서 땅에 접어들었을지도 몰라.”
 78|
 79|“허. 광신도들로도 모자라서 이제는 오랑캐들까지 중원을 넘본다고?”
 80|
 81|“아니, 완전히 정반대일세. 무림맹에 합류하여 암천과 맞서려는 거지. 한데 좀 희한해.”
 82|
 83|“그 말이 사실이라면 다행인 거지, 희한할 건 또 뭔가?”
 84|
 85|“그게…… 그 오랑캐들도 광신도나 다를 바 없다는 소문을 들었거든.”
 86|
 87|“뭐?”
 88|
 89|“그, 뭐라더라? 암천과 맞서 싸우는 것이 성전(聖戰)이니, 대지모신이 굽어보신다느니 별 이상한 소리를 온종일 씨부린다더군.”
 90|
 91|“그게 무슨 병신같은 소린가?”
 92|
 93|“그야 나도 모르지. 연줄을 통해 건너 건너 들은 것뿐인데. 여하튼 모두가 생각하는 것 이상으로 큰일이 벌어지고 있는 건 확실해.”
 94|
 95|대륙은 광활하다. 하지만 직업 특성상 귀가 밝을 수밖에 없는 상인들은 온갖 정보들을 여러 경로로 전해 듣고는 했다.
 96|
 97|그 소문이 진실이든 사실이든 간에, 우선 기억해 놓는다면 언젠가는 큰 재물을 벌어다 줄 수도 있을 테니까.
 98|
 99|그리고 서로를 향해 오가는 대화와 술잔으로 한창 객잔이 시끌벅적해졌을 무렵, 누군가가 잔뜩 취기 어린 목소리로 한마디를 툭 내던졌다.
100|
101|“아, 혹시 그 얘기 들었나? 듣자 하니 상산왕 전하께서 황궁에 머무르고 계신다던데.”
102|
103|“……!”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|찰나의 순간. 후끈하게 달아올랐던 공기가 차갑게 식었다.
108|
109|삽시간에 침묵이 내려앉은 객잔 내부. 이미 모두의 시선은 한 곳을 향해 쏠린 후였다.
110|
111|“어?”
112|
113|갑자기 자신을 향해 쏟아지는 무수한 시선에, 거나하게 취한 와중에도 화들짝 놀란 중년인이 더듬더듬 입을 열었다.
114|
115|“왜, 왜들 그러시오?”
116|
117|그때였다. 순식간에 조용해진 객잔 안의 인파 속에서 몇몇 사람이 입을 연 것은.
118|
119|“지금 뭐라 했소?”
120|
121|“상산왕 전하께서 황궁에 머무르고 계신다고? 봉지(封地)인 산서성이 아니라?”
122|
123|“방금 그 말, 확실한 거요?”
124|
125|모든 재앙은 술과 혀에서 나오는 법.
126|
127|빠르게 빗발치는 질문들에 무언가 잘못되었음을 직감한 중년인은 술이 확 깨는 것을 느꼈다.
128|
129|“사, 사실인지 아닌지는 모르오. 나도 그냥 주워들은 것이라서. 아마도 헛소문이겠지.”
130|
131|“헛소문이라도 좋으니 말해 보시오. 당신이 아는 것 전부.”
132|
133|“아니, 아니오. 아무래도 내가 만취하여 실언한 모양이오. 이만 나가 봐야겠으니 길 좀 비켜 주…….”
134|
135|불콰하게 달아올랐던 안색은 이미 창백해진 지 오래.
136|
137|그러나 비틀거리면서도 용케 자리에서 일어난 중년인은 한 걸음도 채 움직이지 못하고 제자리에 멈춰 서야만 했다.
138|
139|이미 거하게 올라온 술기운 때문이 아닌, 어디선가 뚝 떨어져 내린 물체에 의해서.
140|
141|쿵.
142|
143|제법 큰 소리를 내며 바닥에 내려앉은 그것은 정확히 중년인의 발 앞에 떨어졌고, 동시에 입구를 조이고 있던 가죽끈이 풀리며 안의 내용물을 쏟아냈다.
144|
145|촤르륵.
146|
147|전낭(錢囊)에서 흘러넘친 은자가 흐릿한 불빛을 받아 번쩍였다.
148|
149|언뜻 봐도 서른 냥은 넘어 보이는 액수.
150|
151|그 엄청난 거금에 눈을 부릅뜬 사람들의 귓가로, 나직한 목소리가 파고들었다.
152|
153|“제법 흥미로운 이야기였소.”
154|
155|다시 한번 모두의 고개가 돌아갔다. 아니, 올라갔다.
156|
157|이 층.
158|
159|탁자 하나를 홀로 차지한 어느 젊은 유생이 중년인을 물끄러미 응시하고 있었다.
160|
161|“오십 냥이오. 이 정도면 이야기 값으로는 충분할 듯한데. 귀하는 어찌 생각하는지?”
162|
163|“……!”
164|
165|중년인의 눈꼬리가 파르르 떨렸다.
166|
167|은자 오십 냥이라는 엄청난 액수, 그리고 그런 거금을 툭 내던진 저 젊은 유생에 대한 충격으로.
168|
169|충분?
170|
171|그럴 리가. 충분하다 못해 차고 넘친다.
172|
173|무려 은자 오십 냥이다.
174|
175|항주 운하에서 막일을 하는 그로서는 언감생심 만져 본 적도 없는 거금. 보는 것만으로도 심장이 크게 뛰었다.
176|
177|다만 자신이 조금 전 대수롭지 않게 던진 말이 가져올 결과가, 저 전낭의 무게만큼이나 무겁게 중년인의 마음을 짓눌렀다.
178|
179|“뉘, 뉘십니까요? 일견하기로는 있는 집 자제분 같으신데, 혹시 소인이 뭔가 해서는 안 될 말이라도…….”
180|
181|“걱정할 필요 없소. 그저 궁금할 뿐이니까.”
182|
183|그저 궁금증을 해결하기 위해 은자 오십 냥을?
184|
185|말도 안 되는 소리다.
186|
187|제아무리 있는 집 자식이라지만 그게 말이 되나.
188|
189|젊은 유생의 대답을 들은 중년인은 더욱 큰 불길함에 사로잡혔지만, 인생을 바꿀 기회를 놓칠 수는 없었다.
190|
191|천하의 중심지라 불리는 이 거대한 황도에도 가난뱅이는 있고, 그중 한 사람인 중년인에게 은자 오십 냥은 곧 새로운 삶을 의미했으니까.
192|
193|촤르륵.
194|
195|고민을 끝낸 중년인은 그 틈에 누가 훔쳐 갈세라, 흘러넘친 은자를 허겁지겁 주워 전낭에 집어넣었다. 그리고 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼키며 젊은 유생을 향해 입을 열었다.
196|
197|“새벽 무렵 투전판에 기웃거리다가 이야기를 들었습니다. 며칠 전 북문(北門)을 통해 무려 수백이 넘는 금의위가 입성했다고요. 제아무리 황도라지만 그날따라 대로변의 경계나 분위기가 좀 유별났다고 합디다.”
198|
199|“계속하시오.”
200|
201|“그중 눈치 빠른 몇몇이 이상하다 싶어 불호령을 감수하고 슬쩍 고개를 들었는데, 글쎄 그 무시무시한 금의위들이 마차 한 대를 빽빽하게 에워싸고 있었다지 뭡니까.”
202|
203|“마차?”
204|
205|“예. 그리 화려하지도, 작지도 않은 마차 말입니다. 표물 운송할 때나 쓸 법한 그런 거요.”
206|
207|“그리고 그 마차 안에 상산왕 전하께서 타고 계셨다?”
208|
209|“두 눈으로 똑똑히 봤다고 했습니다. 척 봐도 범상치 않아 보이는 소년의 얼굴이 창가에 나타났는데, 말로만 듣던 그 상산왕 전하가 틀림 없…….”
210|
211|“단지 그것만으로는 부족한 것 같소만.”
212|
213|“예?”
214|
215|중년인의 말을 단칼에 끊어낸 젊은 유생이 말을 이었다.
216|
217|“상산왕 전하께서 황도를 떠나신 지 어언 십 년이 넘었소. 당시에도 워낙 어리셨던 터라 세월이 흐른 지금도 아직 지학(志學. 열다섯 살)도 되지 않은 연배이시지. 한데 새벽까지 투전판이나 기웃거리는 작자가 어찌 그 귀한 분의 얼굴을 알아볼 수 있겠소?”
218|

“……!”

Thud.

Clatter.

“……!”

[P81]

Enough?

[P83]
It was more than enough. It was an absurd amount.

Fifty silver nyang.

That was ridiculous.

[P93]

[P94]
Clatter.

“Pardon?”

That was what Prince Shangshan meant to ordinary people.

A noble, yet pitiful, man.

“……!”

“……!”

[P129]

To escape a fire too great to contain and survive.

Step.

“The Embroidered Uniform Guard…!”

[P160]

[P161]

[P162]

[P163]

[P164]

[P168]
“Loyalty!”

[P171]

[P172]
Bang! Crash!

[P175]

[P177]

[P180]
“What do you think?”

[P182]

[P184]

[P186]

[P187]

[P191]

[P192]

Rustle.

“……!”

[P122]
“……!”

[P123]
For an instant, an invisible shockwave swept through the inn.

[P124]
Sharp intakes of breath broke the silence, and the dim lamplight fell on people frozen in place.

[P125]
The young scholar’s face had gone rigid, too.

[P126]
“An… heir?”

[P127]
“Yes. He didn’t know whether it was the Empress or one of the concubines, but he said she was definitely pregnant.”

[P128]
The young scholar’s gaze darkened.

[P129]
Some of the more than a hundred customers in the inn reacted the same way.

[P130]
The ones biting their lips to hide their shock were poets, scholars, and merchants. Unlike the middle-aged man and a few other simpletons, they understood exactly what those words might mean.

[P131]
*If all of that is true…*

[P132]
The thought alone frightened them.

[P133]
A new heir for an Emperor who’d long had none. And the return of Prince Shangshan, the only direct member of the imperial family to survive the bloodshed more than a decade ago.

[P134]
What could that possibly mean?

[P135]
*A purge…!*

[P136]
A silent scream rang in their heads. Cold sweat had already soaked their backs.

[P137]
They should have left long ago.

[P138]
Whether the rumor was true or not, this was a story they should never have heard.

[P139]
They felt as if they were standing at the edge of a sheer cliff, where one misstep would send them plunging too far to ever climb back.

[P140]
The middle-aged man, meanwhile, was happily counting his silver. He and a few others hadn’t grasped the danger at all.

[P141]
“So His Majesty is finally expecting an heir. What a blessing for the whole country.”

[P142]
“What blessing? The child will inherit the blood of a man who broke the bonds of kinship to take the throne—”

[P143]
“Please, just shut your mouth. Do you have three or four lives to spare? Do you want to get me killed too? If someone reports us, we’re all finished.”

[P144]
“If you’re so afraid of people overhearing, go hide at home. People have always cursed the ruler where he can’t hear them. The Embroidered Uniform Guard aren’t ghosts. What are the chances we’ll run into them? Honestly.”

[P145]
“But what will happen to His Highness, Prince Shangshan?”

[P146]
“What would a nobody like me know? I just hope he stays in the capital from now on. He suffered such terrible things as a child. Who knows what that’s done to him? It’s about time he could live somewhere in peace.”

[P147]
Stories always grew in the telling, and people believed what they wanted to believe.

[P148]
The incredible rumor the middle-aged man had passed on had already become, in the minds of the crowd, a fact backed by solid evidence. A few of those who’d sensed the danger from the start forced their trembling legs to carry them across the noisy inn.

[P149]
Some meant to escape before they were caught in a fire they couldn’t survive.

[P150]
Others meant to confirm the information and use it.

[P151]
But when they reached the entrance, they realized they’d stepped into a mire they could no longer escape.

[P152]
“Where are you all hurrying off to?”

[P153]
At the low voice, the shadows blocking the old doorway stepped forward together.

[P154]
Step.

[P155]
For a moment, it was as if the world had stopped.

[P156]
Those hurrying to leave saw ten men with bamboo hats pulled low—and golden armor flashing beneath their wind-cloaks.

[P157]
“The Embroidered Uniform Guard…!”

[P158]
The words escaped someone’s lips like a scream, and the inn froze.

[P159]
Then the young scholar, who’d been sitting silently in thought, spoke.

[P160]
“That was a truly interesting story. Well worth fifty silver nyang.”

[P161]
The middle-aged man, clutching the pouch full of silver, stared blankly.

[P162]
“Young Master, what on earth is going on…?”

[P163]
“I’m no young master. But I still want to hear more of your story.”

[P164]
“Y-Young Master! You can’t do this! You can’t…!”

[P165]
The young scholar paid no attention to his shouts.

[P166]
The young scholar—no, the hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard—addressed his subordinates at the entrance in a mild voice.

[P167]
“What are you waiting for? Arrest every one of them.”

[P168]
“Loyalty!”

[P169]
With a sharp salute, ten golden figures raced in every direction.

[P170]
Every one of them was a master whose martial arts had reached Supreme First Rate or Peak.

[P171]
Shouts and tearful pleas burst out across the inn. An instant later, the screams of those trying to flee or fight back drowned them out.

[P172]
Bang! Crash!

[P173]
Amid the crashes, the officer pushed off the second-floor railing and landed lightly beside the trembling middle-aged man. He patted him on the shoulder.

[P174]
“Now, it’s noisy here. Let’s go somewhere else and talk. You can tell me what else you know, who fed you that bullshit, and who else has heard it.”

[P175]
He didn’t bother to tell the man what would pay for his story this time.

[P176]
It wouldn’t be silver. But it would shine just as brightly—and be far sharper.

[P177]
* * *

[P178]
After hearing the report, the Emperor remained silent for a long time, even after the messenger withdrew. Only when one other person remained did he finally speak.

[P179]
“What do you think?”

[P180]
From between the dense strings of pearls and the silks drifting around them, someone answered.

[P181]
“Someone must have spread the rumor deliberately.”

[P182]
“Who?”

[P183]
“Isn’t it obvious? The East Depot, Jin Taekyung—the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—or… both.”

[P184]
“They’ve joined forces?”

[P185]
“That’s the only possibility for now.”

[P186]
“I’m beginning to regret it. Perhaps I shouldn’t have listened to you and let Jin Taekyung into the imperial palace.”

[P187]
The Emperor clicked his tongue and murmured, almost to himself.

[P188]
“Did the person who sent you to me foresee this, too?”

[P189]
Someone beyond the silks answered.

[P190]
“That person is greater and wiser than anyone I know. But Jin Taekyung is unpredictable. He cannot be easily judged.”

[P191]
Without realizing it, the Emperor nodded.

[P192]
Jin Taekyung’s audacity was impossible to fathom. So were his martial prowess and his convictions.

[P193]
Whatever their respective positions, the Jin Taekyung he’d seen the day before had been enough to make even the Emperor let out an incredulous laugh.

[P194]
“We’d better rein him in before he jeopardizes the great undertaking. And what of the target?”

[P195]
“It won’t be easy. Not at present.”

[P196]
“Of course. If it were easy, he wouldn’t have been a thorn in our side for more than ten years. But the Great Nation cannot be set right until he’s gone. You must see it done.”

[P197]
Rustle.

[P198]
In place of an answer, a faint breeze stirred the silks.

[P199]
The Emperor realized that the person who’d been there only moments ago had vanished. He gave a bitter smile and muttered,

[P200]
“The rumor’s already out. There’s no point trying to hide it now. We’ll have to make it true.”

[P201]
It was the moment that heralded a grand celebration of the birth of a new heir to inherit the Great Nation.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

Thud.

Clatter.

“……!”

[P81]

Enough?

It was more than enough. It was an absurd amount.

Fifty silver nyang.

That was ridiculous.

[P91]

[P93]

[P94]
Clatter.

“Pardon?”

A noble, yet pitiful, man.

“……!”

To escape a fire too great to contain and survive.

Step.

“The Embroidered Uniform Guard…!”

[P160]

[P161]

[P162]

[P163]

[P164]

[P165]

[P167]

[P168]
“Loyalty!”

[P172]
Bang! Crash!

[P174]

[P175]
He didn’t bother to tell the man.

[P177]

[P180]
“What do you think?”

[P182]
“Someone must have deliberately spread the rumor.”

[P183]
“Who’s behind it?”

[P184]

[P185]

[P186]

[P187]

[P189]

[P190]

[P191]

[P192]

[P193]

Rustle.

[P126]
“An… heir?”

[P127]
“Yes. He didn’t know whether it was the Empress or one of the concubines, but he said she was definitely pregnant.”

[P128]
The young scholar’s gaze darkened.

[P129]
Some of the more than a hundred customers in the inn reacted the same way.

[P130]
The ones biting their lips to hide their shock were poets, scholars, and merchants. Unlike the middle-aged man and a few other simpletons, they understood exactly what those words might mean.

[P131]
*If all of that is true…*

[P132]
The thought alone frightened them.

[P133]
A new heir for an Emperor who’d long had none. And the return of Prince Shangshan, the only direct member of the imperial family to survive the bloodshed more than a decade ago.

[P134]
What could that possibly mean?

[P135]
*A purge…!*

[P136]
A silent scream rang in their heads. Cold sweat had already soaked their backs.

[P137]
They should have left long ago.

[P138]
Whether the rumor was true or not, this was a story they should never have heard.

[P139]
They felt as if they were standing at the edge of a sheer cliff, where one misstep would send them plunging too far to ever climb back.

[P140]
The middle-aged man, meanwhile, was happily counting his silver. He and a few others hadn’t grasped the danger at all.

[P141]
“So His Majesty is finally expecting an heir. What a blessing for the whole country.”

[P142]
“What blessing? The child will inherit the blood of a man who broke the bonds of kinship to take the throne—”

[P143]
“Please, just shut your mouth. Do you have three or four lives to spare? Do you want to get me killed too? If someone reports us, we’re all finished.”

[P144]
“If you’re so afraid of people overhearing, go hide at home. People have always cursed the ruler where he can’t hear them. The Embroidered Uniform Guard aren’t ghosts. What are the chances we’ll run into them? Honestly.”

[P145]
“But what will happen to His Highness, Prince Shangshan?”

[P146]
“What would a nobody like me know? I just hope he stays in the capital from now on. He suffered such terrible things as a child. Who knows what that’s done to him? It’s about time he could live somewhere in peace.”

[P147]
Stories always grew in the telling, and people believed what they wanted to believe.

[P148]
The incredible rumor the middle-aged man had passed on had already become, in the minds of the crowd, a fact backed by solid evidence. A few of those who’d sensed the danger from the start forced their trembling legs to carry them across the noisy inn.

[P149]
Some meant to escape before they were caught in a fire they couldn’t survive.

[P150]
Others meant to confirm the information and use it.

[P151]
But when they reached the entrance, they realized they’d stepped into a mire they could no longer escape.

[P152]
“Where are you all hurrying off to?”

[P153]
At the low voice, the shadows blocking the old doorway stepped forward together.

[P154]
Step.

[P155]
For a moment, it was as if the world had stopped.

[P156]
Those hurrying to leave saw ten men with bamboo hats pulled low—and golden armor flashing beneath their wind-cloaks.

[P157]
“The Embroidered Uniform Guard…!”

[P158]
The words escaped someone’s lips like a scream, and the inn froze.

[P159]
Then the young scholar, who’d been sitting silently in thought, spoke.

[P160]
“That was a truly interesting story. Well worth fifty silver nyang.”

[P161]
The middle-aged man, clutching the pouch full of silver, stared blankly.

[P162]
“Young Master, what on earth is going on…?”

[P163]
“I’m no young master. But I still want to hear more of your story.”

[P164]
“Y-Young Master! You can’t do this! You can’t…!”

[P165]
The young scholar paid no attention to his shouts.

[P166]
The young scholar—no, the hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard—addressed his subordinates at the entrance in a mild voice.

[P167]
“What are you waiting for? Arrest every one of them.”

[P168]
“Loyalty!”

[P169]
With a sharp salute, ten golden figures raced in every direction.

[P170]
Every one of them was a master whose martial arts had reached Supreme First Rate or Peak.

[P171]
Shouts and tearful pleas burst out across the inn. An instant later, the screams of those trying to flee or fight back drowned them out.

[P172]
Bang! Crash!

[P173]
Amid the crashes, the officer pushed off the second-floor railing and landed lightly beside the trembling middle-aged man. He patted him on the shoulder.

[P174]
“Now, it’s noisy here. Let’s go somewhere else and talk. You can tell me what else you know, who fed you that bullshit, and who else has heard it.”

[P175]
He didn’t bother to tell the man what would pay for his story this time.

[P176]
It wouldn’t be silver. But it would shine just as brightly—and be far sharper.

[P177]
* * *

[P178]
After hearing the report, the Emperor remained silent for a long time, even after the messenger withdrew. Only when one other person remained did he finally speak.

[P179]
“What do you think?”

[P180]
From between the dense strings of pearls and the silks drifting around them, someone answered.

[P181]
“Someone must have spread the rumor deliberately.”

[P182]
“Who?”

[P183]
“Isn’t it obvious? The East Depot, Jin Taekyung—the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—or… both.”

[P184]
“They’ve joined forces?”

[P185]
“That’s the only possibility for now.”

[P186]
“I’m beginning to regret it. Perhaps I shouldn’t have listened to you and let Jin Taekyung into the imperial palace.”

[P187]
The Emperor clicked his tongue and murmured, almost to himself.

[P188]
“Did the person who sent you to me foresee this, too?”

[P189]
Someone beyond the silks answered.

[P190]
“That person is greater and wiser than anyone I know. But Jin Taekyung is unpredictable. He cannot be easily judged.”

[P191]
Without realizing it, the Emperor nodded.

[P192]
Jin Taekyung’s audacity was impossible to fathom. So were his martial prowess and his convictions.

[P193]
Whatever their respective positions, the Jin Taekyung he’d seen the day before had been enough to make even the Emperor let out an incredulous laugh.

[P194]
“We’d better rein him in before he jeopardizes the great undertaking. And what of the target?”

[P195]
“It won’t be easy. Not at present.”

[P196]
“Of course. If it were easy, he wouldn’t have been a thorn in our side for more than ten years. But the Great Nation cannot be set right until he’s gone. You must see it done.”

[P197]
Rustle.

[P198]
In place of an answer, a faint breeze stirred the silks.

[P199]
The Emperor realized that the person who’d been there only moments ago had vanished. He gave a bitter smile and muttered,

[P200]
“The rumor’s already out. There’s no point trying to hide it now. We’ll have to make it true.”

[P201]
It was the moment that heralded a grand celebration of the birth of a new heir to inherit the Great Nation.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P54]

“Huh?”

[P64]

Thud.

Clatter.

Enough?

Fifty silver nyang.

[P94]
Clatter.

The inn had been bustling with noise only moments ago. Now it was as quiet as a grave.

That was what Prince Shangshan meant to ordinary people.

[P111]
Noble, yet pitiable.

“……!”

[P122]
“……!”

[P124]

The young scholar’s face had gone rigid, too.

The young scholar’s gaze darkened.

Some of the more than a hundred customers in the inn reacted the same way.

Stories always grew in the telling, and people believed what they wanted to believe.

[P149]
Some meant to escape before they were caught in a fire they couldn’t survive.

[P150]

[P152]
“Where are you all hurrying off to?”

[P153]
At the low voice, the shadows blocking the old doorway stepped forward together.

[P154]
Step.

[P155]
For a moment, it was as if the world had stopped.

[P156]

[P157]
“The Embroidered Uniform Guard…!”

[P158]
The words escaped someone’s lips like a scream, and the inn froze.

[P159]
Then the young scholar, who’d been sitting silently in thought, spoke.

[P160]
“That was a truly interesting story. Well worth fifty silver nyang.”

[P161]
The middle-aged man, clutching the pouch full of silver, stared blankly.

[P162]
“Young Master, what on earth is going on…?”

[P163]
“I’m no young master. But I still want to hear more of your story.”

[P164]
“Y-Young Master! You can’t do this! You can’t…!”

[P165]
The young scholar paid no attention to his shouts.

[P166]
The young scholar—no, the hundred-household officer of the Embroidered Uniform Guard—addressed his subordinates at the entrance in a mild voice.

[P167]
“What are you waiting for? Arrest every one of them.”

[P168]
“Loyalty!”

[P169]
With a sharp salute, ten golden figures raced in every direction.

[P170]
Every one of them was a master whose martial arts had reached Supreme First Rate or Peak.

[P171]
Shouts and tearful pleas burst out across the inn. An instant later, the screams of those trying to flee or fight back drowned them out.

[P172]
Bang! Crash!

[P173]
Amid the crashes, the officer pushed off the second-floor railing and landed lightly beside the trembling middle-aged man. He patted him on the shoulder.

[P174]
“Now, it’s noisy here. Let’s go somewhere else and talk. You can tell me what else you know, who fed you that bullshit, and who else has heard it.”

[P175]
He didn’t bother to tell the man what would pay for his story this time.

[P176]
It wouldn’t be silver. But it would shine just as brightly—and be far sharper.

[P177]
* * *

[P178]
After hearing the report, the Emperor remained silent for a long time, even after the messenger withdrew. Only when one other person remained did he finally speak.

[P179]
“What do you think?”

[P180]
From between the dense strings of pearls and the silks drifting around them, someone answered.

[P181]
“Someone must have spread the rumor deliberately.”

[P182]
“Who?”

[P183]
“Isn’t it obvious? The East Depot, Jin Taekyung—the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon—or… both.”

[P184]
“They’ve joined forces?”

[P185]
“That’s the only possibility for now.”

[P186]
“I’m beginning to regret it. Perhaps I shouldn’t have listened to you and let Jin Taekyung into the imperial palace.”

[P187]

[P188]

[P189]
Someone beyond the silks answered.

[P190]

[P191]

[P192]
Jin Taekyung’s audacity was impossible to fathom. So were his martial prowess and his convictions.

[P193]
Whatever their respective positions, the Jin Taekyung he’d seen the day before had been enough to make even the Emperor let out an incredulous laugh.

[P194]
“We’d better rein him in before he jeopardizes the great undertaking. And what of the target?”

[P195]
“It won’t be easy. Not at present.”

[P196]
“Of course. If it were easy, he wouldn’t have been a thorn in our side for more than ten years. But the Great Nation cannot be set right until he’s gone. You must see it done.”

[P197]
Rustle.

[P198]
In place of an answer, a faint breeze stirred the silks.

[P199]
The Emperor realized that the person who’d been there only moments ago had vanished. He gave a bitter smile and muttered,

[P200]

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
